deep.reconstruction:
Setting (cote 154, 1983-84): Σ is a finite system of pseudo-lines in the projective plane X, and S is its set of vertices. Grothendieck studies the set P = Pr(Σ) of combinatorial 'positions' of an additional pseudo-line D relative to Σ, and the graph Γ = Γ(Σ) whose edges are immediate specializations/generalizations between positions.

The position types are:
- stable: card(S∩D) = 0;
- semi-stable: card(S∩D) = 1;
- more special positions: D passes through two or more vertices.

When D moves through a vertex, a small triangle of Σ' = Σ ∪ {D} shrinks to a point; such a triangle is a 'triangle of specialization'.

On the previous page he set up a local polygonal structure at each vertex D of Γ. The arcs of Γ issuing from D are identified with Sp_0(D) ⊔ Cerc_0(D), seen as open arcs and points on the circle D̃. He tries to prove that this set always has at least 3 elements, so that Γ is locally like a polygonal surface. This amounts to:
- at least 3 specialization triangles when D is stable;
- at least 1 when D is semi-stable.

This page first fixes an omission in the list of vertices of Γ. The 'most important' positions are those where D coincides with a line Δ of Σ itself. In matroid terms this is a non-simple extension, with D parallel to Δ. He then describes the immediate specializations onto such a Δ:
- They can only come from a semi-stable position D with S∩D = {o}, where o must be a vertex lying on Δ.
- There must also be a global triangular sector of X, bounded by D and Δ, which is a 'cuvette' (a bowl: a sector containing no obstruction). D can rotate about o through this sector onto Δ. He calls it a 'cuvette de spécialisation'.
- There can be one such cuvette on each side of D∖{o}.
- He decrees that cuvettes count as 'equivalent' to specialization triangles for D.

The left column continues case (b), the semi-stable case of the degree argument. D' is a specialization in which vertex a slides onto an edge bc. D' has at least two other specialization triangles with base on D', meeting (b,c) in at most a vertex. If one of them works, the argument succeeds; otherwise the configuration of the figure arises.

He then notes there is in fact a counterexample, with Σ = St_{4,3} (?): a non-stable position with no specialization triangle at all. That is precisely why the cuvettes, i.e. specializations to lines of Σ, must be added as extra neighbours.

The large figure shows D (green), Δ (orange, through o) and the hatched cuvette sector. The aim is to show that the poset of positions, including the lines of Σ, carries a 2-dimensional polygonal (cell-complex / surface) structure. In modern terms this is the extension space of the rank-3 oriented matroid of Σ, which one expects to be a 2-sphere-like object.
errors: The previous page's claim that a semi-stable D always has at least one specialization triangle is false. Grothendieck finds the counterexample himself (Σ = St_{4,3}?) and repairs the claim by counting 'cuvettes' (specializations onto lines Δ of Σ) as equivalent to triangles.
The argument in the left column is visibly incomplete ('Sinon, on a la figure'); no complete proof of the degree ≥ 3 / polygon-link property appears on this page.

ideas.what: Space/poset of positions of an extra pseudo-line relative to an arrangement, with specialization order and graph Γ
ideas.modern_name: Extension space (poset of single-element extensions) of a rank-3 oriented matroid; 'MacPhersonian'-type combinatorial Grassmannian of extensions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Las Vergnas (single-element extensions, 1978); Sturmfels–Ziegler, 'Extension spaces of oriented matroids' (1993); extension space conjecture (Mnëv–Ziegler era; counterexample by G. Liu, ca. 2017-2020)

ideas.what: Including the lines of Σ themselves as positions (D coinciding with Δ), reached via 'cuvettes de spécialisation', to make the local structure polygonal
ideas.modern_name: Non-simple (parallel-element) extensions in the extension poset; needed to close up the extension cell complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in oriented matroid extension theory (Las Vergnas, Bachem–Kern, Sturmfels–Ziegler)

ideas.what: Local link condition: the set of immediate specializations/generalizations of a position forms a polygon with at least 3 sides
ideas.modern_name: Showing a cell complex is a 2-manifold via polygonal vertex links / triangle-flip (mutation) count
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (mutations of pseudoline arrangements: Ringel 1956; Levi's lemma, triangle counts)

missed.claim: Grothendieck is attempting a direct combinatorial proof that the poset of positions of a pseudo-line relative to an arbitrary pseudo-line system (non-realizable included) is a polygonal 2-dimensional complex, presumably a sphere. This is the rank-3 case of what later became the extension space problem. The page shows the naive degree argument failing and the fix by adding parallel positions (cuvettes).
missed.quote: j'ai oublié les cas les plus importants ... correspondant aux droites de Σ elles-mêmes ! ... on considère les cuvettes de spécialisations pour D, comme "équivalentes" à un triangle de sp. pour D.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The rank-3 extension space was treated by Sturmfels–Ziegler (1993). Grothendieck's independent, earlier, manifold-link-style approach is historically notable, though not mathematically new given that later work.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an independent, early (1983-84) attack on the topology of the rank-3 extension space of pseudo-line arrangements, a topic later formalized by Sturmfels–Ziegler. The content on this page is exploratory, with a self-found counterexample and a local fix, and contains no finished result beyond the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'les p.v. surconstrictiques' is uncertain. It is likely 'les positions super-...' or 'supercritiques' (underlined), referring to positions where D coincides with a line of Σ.

'Il est clair qu'elles ne doivent se faire (au moins des spécialisations immédiates) : position d'une position stable qui contiennent' should read roughly 'ne peuvent se faire (au moins les spécialisations immédiates) qu'à partir d'une position semi-stable qui contient o — i.e. D semi-stable'. The struck marginal words are 'mais si !'.
'Soit S∩D={o}, il faut que Δ. soit un sommet de' should read 'Soit S∩D={o}, il faut que o soit un sommet de Δ'.
'conduit ... finissions' at the bottom left is likely 'et conduit à ... de spécialisation ... finis' (uncertain); 'St_{4,3}' is also uncertain.
